samples.summary: The paste path that writes whole table cells (`pasteTableCells`) bypasses the new `capTableNesting` producer guard
samples.evidence: `applyPastePlan` (text-editor.ts:1575) routes a clipboard payload to one of two writers: `pasteTableCells(plan.cells)` or `insertBlocks(plan.blocks)`. Only `insertBlocks` was changed to call `capTableNesting(incoming, this.doc.tableNestingDepth(pos.blockId))` (text-editor.ts:4568-4573). `pasteTableCells` clones the incoming `TableCell`s verbatim into the target cells (text-editor.ts:4716-4718 and 4748-4749) with no depth check, and those cells may hold nested tables: `getSelectedTableCells` copies the real `cell.blocks` (including nested table blocks) into the waffledocs payload, and `deserializeClipboard`'s sanitizer only bounds the *fragment* at `MAX_TABLE_DEPTH = 8` (clipboard.ts:72,309). Pasting such a cell rectangle into a cell already near the ceiling produces a model past `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`, which the store then writes as a table with zero rows (silent loss of the pasted content in the CRDT while the local cache still shows it) and which later makes `writeFullDocument`/`writeDocsRoot` refuse the document entirely. The fix belongs at this site (cap the cells' blocks against `doc.tableNestingDepth` of the target cell), not on the new code.

samples.summary: The bounded merge expansion in `normalizeCellRange` also reaches write paths, contrary to the new doc comment that says only the painter passes a budget
samples.evidence: `selection.ts:214` now always passes `MAX_MERGE_EXPANSION_CELLS` inside `normalizeCellRange`, and `normalizeCellRange` is reached from `Selection.getNormalizedRange` — which is not only the painter. `text-editor.ts:4165-4185` uses `getNormalizedRange(...).tableCellRange` to clear the contents of every selected cell and then `doc.updateBlockDirect`, and `text-editor.ts:4322-4325` (`getSelectedTableCells`, feeding copy/cut) uses the same rectangle. On a table large enough to exhaust the budget these writes act on a partially-expanded rectangle: delete skips cells it used to clear, and cut/copy returns a short rectangle — exactly the 'stopped growing early' outcome the new comment in selection.ts:21-48 says is confined to the render path. Either the budget must not apply to `getNormalizedRange` consumers that write, or the comment's claim is wrong.

samples.summary: Tightening the docs body depth check from `> MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH` to `>= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` makes previously-accepted bodies a 400, breaking the documented GET → PUT round-trip for already-stored deep documents
samples.evidence: `docs/design/rest-api.md:457` states '`GET` → edit → `PUT` stays lossless for docs bodies'. For a document that already holds a table at nesting depth 32 (accepted by the old `> 32` check, or written by any earlier producer), `GET /content` now returns that table truncated to `rows: []` and a `PUT` of the very body just returned is rejected with 400 'blocks are nested too deeply' by this check. Out-of-diff consumers affected: the CLI's `docs content write` / `--replace` (packages/cli/src/docs/content.ts) and any API client doing read-modify-write. The doc statement at docs/design/rest-api.md:452-460 is now also out of step (the cap for docs bodies is `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`, not `MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH`).

samples.summary: `writeFullDocument`'s new unconditional throw is reachable from header/footer edits and from import apply, where nothing catches it
samples.evidence: The refusal added at yorkie-doc-store.ts:3330-3346 fires for a document whose *body* holds a table at the cap, but two unrelated operations funnel through it: `setHeader` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:962) and `setFooter` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1001) on the treeless path, and `store.setDocument` at packages/frontend/src/app/documents/apply-imported-content.ts:226 / packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:396. For a legacy or peer-written document already past the cap this makes every header/footer edit throw an uncaught error out of the toolbar handler rather than degrade — the 'one thing lost is the edit' claim in the docstring holds only if the caller catches, and neither `setHeader` caller nor `applyImportedContent` does. Worth confirming whether the docs header/footer UI has an error boundary around these calls.

samples.summary: `hasDocsTableAtNestingCap` is exported but only used inside its own module, which knip's unused-export check covers for packages/backend
samples.evidence: knip.json:21-28 lists `packages/backend` with `project: ["src/**/*.ts"]` and entries limited to `src/main.ts`, tests and seed templates. `hasDocsTableAtNestingCap` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:231) is referenced only at lines 240, 252-254 of the same file; `documentHasTableAtNestingCap` is the one the copy service imports. Dropping the `export` avoids an unused-export report.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. `applyPastePlan` (text-editor.ts:1575-1576) routes to two writers; only `insertBlocks` gained the cap (text-editor.ts:4568-4572). `pasteTableCells` (text-editor.ts:4698-4755) clones incoming cells verbatim (4716-4717, 4748-4749) and persists via `doc.updateBlockDirect` (4755), which forwards straight to `store.updateBlock` with no depth check (model/document.ts:793-796) — unlike `insertBlockAfter`, which does carry the `tableNestingDepth` refusal (document.ts:925-928). The pasted cells can hold nested tables: `cloneTableCells` spreads each block keeping `tableData` (clipboard.ts:477-491), and `deserializeClipboard` sanitizes cell rows only against the fragment-relative `MAX_TABLE_DEPTH = 8` (clipboard.ts:72, 309, 470), which `capTableNesting`'s own doc comment states is insufficient without the target depth (clipboard.ts:419-427). The internal-clipboard entry point reaching this writer is text-editor.ts:1753-1759. Downstream, `YorkieDocStore.updateBlock` builds at the target path's depth (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1756) and `buildBlockNode` emits a table at/past `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` with zero rows (yorkie-doc-store.ts:398-400) while the local cache keeps the full block (1760-1761), and `writeFullDocument` afterwards refuses the whole document (yorkie-doc-store.ts:3330-3341). No guard on any caller prevents this path. Blast-radius lane: a newly added producer guard with a reachable sibling writer that bypasses it; major impact (silent CRDT content loss plus a document the full-document writer rejects).

verdict.reason: Code is present exactly as described. selection.ts:213-215 always applies MAX_MERGE_EXPANSION_CELLS inside normalizeCellRange, which selection.ts:264 invokes from normalizeRange, which selection.ts:874-879 (getNormalizedRange) exposes to all consumers — not just computeSelectionRects. Non-render consumers act on that rectangle: text-editor.ts:4165-4185 clears every cell in the rectangle and calls doc.updateBlockDirect (a write), text-editor.ts:4322-4347 builds the copy/cut payload from it, and selection.ts:891-897 builds copied text from it. The new doc comments at selection.ts:25-32 and selection.ts:111-116 assert the budget touches only a caller that 'paints rather than acts' and that 'every other caller feeds the result to a write' — that contract statement is false for these consumers. I could not refute as already-guarded: although the drag/Shift+Arrow handlers pre-expand unbounded (text-editor.ts:3324, 3967, 3991), nothing enforces that the stored rectangle is at fixed point — table-merge-context.ts:27-31 states programmatic setRange callers are not required to expand, and editor.ts:2490-2496 restores an undo/redo tableCellRange verbatim into setRange after structural changes. In those cases the bounded read-time expansion is the only canonicalisation, so a partially expanded rectangle reaches a write and the clipboard. This is a behaviour change to a shared symbol whose non-diff consumers were not considered — in this lens's lane, and blocking at major (writes skip cells / copy returns a short rectangle).

finding.summary: `writeFullDocument`'s new unconditional throw is reachable from header/footer edits and from import apply, where nothing catches it
finding.evidence: The refusal added at yorkie-doc-store.ts:3330-3346 fires for a document whose *body* holds a table at the cap, but two unrelated operations funnel through it: `setHeader` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:962) and `setFooter` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1001) on the treeless path, and `store.setDocument` at packages/frontend/src/app/documents/apply-imported-content.ts:226 / packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:396. For a legacy or peer-written document already past the cap this makes every header/footer edit throw an uncaught error out of the toolbar handler rather than degrade — the 'one thing lost is the edit' claim in the docstring holds only if the caller catches, and neither `setHeader` caller nor `applyImportedContent` does. Worth confirming whether the docs header/footer UI has an error boundary around these calls.

verdict.reason: The guard at yorkie-doc-store.ts:3330-3341 exists as described, but none of the three "uncaught" sites the finding names hold up. (a) docs-view.tsx:396 is inside an explicit try/catch (395-407) that logs and leaves the pending import for retry. (b) apply-imported-content.ts:226 propagates by design ("either lands or throws", documented at apply-imported-content.ts:181-184), and both callers catch it: upload-queue.ts:444/452-465 patches the item to status "error" with the message, and miro-import-runner.ts:190 and :225 catch, clean up the orphan doc, and report. (c) setHeader:962 / setFooter:1001 call writeFullDocument only on the treeless branch (960/999), and on a treeless root getDocument() returns `{ blocks: [] }` (859-863) — remote changes set dirty=true (810) so no stale rich cache can be served — so a document "already past the cap" necessarily has a Tree and takes the granular editByPath path (968-985 / 1007-1026), never writeFullDocument. The sole caller, Doc.ensureHeader/ensureFooter (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:219-240), passes a single empty block, so the header/footer arms of the guard cannot fire either. Each claimed uncaught/reachable path is either guarded by an existing catch or unreachable under the stated scenario.

mergedFrom.summary: `buildRowNode` / `buildCellNode` gained a REQUIRED `depth: number` parameter, but three existing call sites still pass one argument

finding.summary: The new nesting cap only guards full-document writes; every incremental block/row/cell write enters `buildBlockNode` at depth 0 and can write past `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`
finding.evidence: `buildBlockNode(block)` (depth 0) is called from paths that write at an ARBITRARY tree depth: `updateBlock` → `tree.editByPath(blockPath, endPath, buildBlockNode(block))` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1723, where `resolveBlockTreePath` resolves paths inside table cells — see `isCellBlockPath` at :1701), `insertBlockAfter` (:2335), the paste path `insertBlocksAfter` (:2371), `insertBlock` (:2312), plus the row/cell writers at :2775/:2818/:2858. So a table block inserted into a cell that is already 30 tables deep is written with its own subtree counted from 0, producing CRDT content deeper than `treeNodeToBlock` will ever materialize (packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:225) — exactly the state `writeFullDocument`'s new refusal says must never exist. The user-facing route is unguarded too: `Doc.insertTableInCell()` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:885) calls `store.insertBlockAfter` with no depth check, and grep finds no nesting check anywhere on the editor's insert-table-in-cell path (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4237).

verdict.reason: The finding describes code that does not exist in this tree. `buildBlockNode` takes a REQUIRED `depth` parameter with no default (yorkie-doc-store.ts:386), documented at :375-381 as required specifically so incremental writers cannot restart the counter at 0. Every path the finding names passes a computed depth: `updateBlock` passes `blockPathNestingDepth(blockPath, region)` (:1753-1757), `insertBlockAfter` passes it for the sibling path (:2373-2377), the paste path `insertBlocksAfter` computes `siblingDepth` once and maps it (:2415-2416), and the row/cell writers use `resolveTableRowDepth` = `blockPathNestingDepth(path, region) + 1` (:2785-2794) at `insertTableRow` (:2844-2845), `insertTableColumn` (:2877,:2888) and `updateTableCell` (:2927-2928). Even `splitBlock`, which cannot produce a table, passes `blockDepth` (:2499,:2560,:2634) so no call site in the file omits it. The only depth-0 incremental call is `insertBlock` (:2336-2347), which is a body top-level insert by array index where depth 0 is correct. The claimed user-facing bypass is also absent: `Doc.insertTableInCell` throws at `tableNestingDepth(blockId) >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH` (document.ts:925-930), and the editor declines before splitting (editor.ts:4232-4234). The reviewer's quoted call shape `buildBlockNode(block)` would not even type-check against the current signature.

finding.summary: The backend's twin writer (`writeDocsRoot`) has no nesting cap, and `PUT /content` admits one level deeper than the readers materialize
finding.evidence: `packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:150-200` is the documented mirror of `writeFullDocument` ( see its own comment at :302) but `buildBlockNode`/`buildRowNode`/`buildCellNode` there recurse with no depth parameter and `writeDocsRoot` (:306) has no equivalent of the new `hasTableAtNestingCap` refusal. `PUT /content` reaches it with a caller-supplied body (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:213), and its validator allows `depth > MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH` only (`assertValidBlock`, :443, with `MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH = 32` at :806) — a table at nesting depth 32 passes, while `treeNodeToBlock` truncates any table at `depth >= 32` to `rows: []` (packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:225). So the API can persist a document whose deepest table no reader shows, and which the frontend now *refuses* to rewrite at all (`writeFullDocument` throws), i.e. a document that can neither be read nor repaired. The backend also duplicates the constant instead of importing `MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH`, so the two will drift.

verdict.reason: The code is not as described. (1) The backend writers DO thread a depth counter and cap: `buildBlockNode(block, depth)` at docs-tree.ts:162 caps at :179 (`depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH ? [] : rows.map(row => buildRowNode(row, depth + 1))`), with `buildCellNode(cell, depth)` :201 and `buildRowNode(row, depth)` :211, seeded at 0 from :268/:272/:278. (2) `writeDocsRoot` (docs-tree.ts:372) DOES carry the refusal: its first statement at :376-382 throws when `documentHasTableAtNestingCap(document)` (:250, delegating to `hasDocsTableAtNestingCap` :231-245 over blocks/header/footer) is true. (3) The constant is NOT duplicated — it is imported from `@wafflebase/docs` at docs-tree.ts:38, defined once in packages/docs/src/model/table-nesting.ts:26 and re-exported at packages/docs/src/index.ts:97. (4) The validator does NOT check only `depth > MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH`: `assertValidBlock` (docs-content.controller.ts:439) refuses at :454 with `if (depth >= MAX_TABLE_NESTING_DEPTH)`, using the shared constant imported at :49; `MAX_ELEMENT_DEPTH` (:817) remains only for the separate element walk (:851, :1191). Consequently the claimed PUT /content path (controller:213 -> writeDocsRoot) cannot persist a table at or past depth 32: it 400s at the validator and, failing that, throws at the writer. The asserted unguarded twin writer does not exist in this tree.

finding.summary: Document copy does the exact read-truncate-then-full-rewrite the new guard declares unsafe, with no guard on the backend side
finding.evidence: `readDocsRoot(doc.getRoot())` (packages/backend/src/document/document-copy.service.ts:428) returns the model produced by the capped `docsTreeToDocument`, and the result is handed straight to `writeDocsRoot(root as DocsYorkieRoot, rewritten)` (:445). That is the pattern the delta's own comment says must be refused ("rewriting the whole tree from that model would push the truncation into the CRDT"), but the backend path has no `hasTableAtNestingCap` check, so a copy of a deeply nested document silently drops every row the reader declined to descend into. Same pattern in `packages/backend/src/template/seed/seed-templates.ts:79`.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts the backend copy path has no nesting-cap check and silently truncates. That code is not present as described. document-copy.service.ts:446 explicitly calls `documentHasTableAtNestingCap(content)` between the `readDocsRoot` read (:429) and the `writeDocsRoot` write (:459) and throws BadRequestException (:447-450), with the accompanying comment at :439-445 stating the exact rationale the finding says is missing; the helper is imported at :12. Independently, `writeDocsRoot` itself refuses the condition unconditionally at packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:376-382, so no caller can perform the read-truncate-rewrite. The second cited site, packages/backend/src/template/seed/seed-templates.ts:79, calls `writeDocsRoot` (imported at :14) and therefore hits that same refusal — it is already guarded. `documentHasTableAtNestingCap` (docs-tree.ts:250-256) covers blocks, header and footer.

finding.summary: The new `MAX_MERGE_EXPANSION_CELLS` budget also truncates expansion on WRITE paths (cell merge), not only the paint path its comment describes
finding.evidence: `computeTableMergeContext` calls `expandCellRangeForMerges` (packages/docs/src/view/table-merge-context.ts:53) and returns the expanded rectangle as the merge range; `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4384` builds the context and :4366 executes `doc.mergeCells(tableBlockId, range)` with it. Shift+drag selection also expands at write time (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:3324, :3967, :3991). The new doc comment in selection.ts justifies the budget as "a merge at its edge paints short", but on a table large enough to exhaust it the *merge command* would operate on a partially expanded rectangle and can cut through an existing merge, persisting a malformed table to the CRDT rather than merely painting short.

verdict.reason: The finding asserts that MAX_MERGE_EXPANSION_CELLS truncates expansion on the write/merge paths. It does not. `expandCellRangeForMerges` takes the budget as an opt-in third parameter defaulting to `Infinity` (selection.ts:118-122), and the budget constant is passed at exactly one call site — `normalizeCellRange` (selection.ts:214), the render/presence path. The merge-command path named in the finding calls it with two arguments, i.e. unbounded: `table-merge-context.ts:53` (`expandCellRangeForMerges(cr, tableData)`), whose result flows to `editor.ts:4374` `doc.mergeCells(tableBlockId, range)`. The shift+drag/shift+arrow write-time sites cited by the reviewer (text-editor.ts:3324-3331, 3967-3974, 3991-3994) are likewise all two-argument, unbounded calls. The truncated rectangle also cannot reach the merge path indirectly: `editor.ts:4392` passes `selection.range`, the raw range stored by `Selection.setRange` (selection.ts:855-856); `normalizeCellRange` is reached only from `normalizeRange` (selection.ts:264), which returns a NEW derived object and never writes back into `this.range`. So no merge write ever sees a partially expanded rectangle from this budget. I also checked the nearest true variant before refuting — the budgeted rectangle does reach the cell-clear loop at text-editor.ts:4169-4185 via `getNormalizedRange` — but that path only clears cell content inside the rectangle and skips covered cells (`cell.colSpan === 0`, line 4176); truncation there clears less, it writes no merge geometry, so it is not the CRDT-corrupting merge defect the finding asserts. The code is not as described.
